text: No, the June 2025 finding is no longer valid. As of November 2026, a tree-cover loss event of 13.5 ha (3.91% of the asset) was detected in 2025 within the property. However, this is still pending corroboration—meaning it requires confirmation in later data to rule out temporary loss (e.g., harvesting that may regrow). The 2025 due-diligence report was correct for its time (no loss detected through 2024), but new evidence shows a subsequent change. The cause (e.g., logging, fire) and legality remain unknown.
